description.narrative: Strengthening social dialogue in GAP factories in Bangladesh
Strengthening social dialogue in GAP factories in Bangladesh
The project aims at building and strengthening the capacity of the national tripartite constituents of Bangladesh through the newly established ILO-BW Learning Hub

title.narrative: Output 1.4. Strengthened social dialogue and labour relations laws, processes and institutions

description.narrative:
1. Capacitated 27 paralegals (8 women) to support workers and employers to resolve enterprise level disputes. From Jan. 2020-July 2021, the Paralegals attended to 948 enterprise level worker complaints from approx. 600 enterprises involving over 11K+ workers (52% female and 48% male) and successfully resolved 56% (527) cases. Grievance handling mechanisms were established in a total of 206 factories.
2. A. i. During 2020-21, the Workers Resource Centre (WRC) outreached 78 unionized factories to provide training on Collective Bargaining and Negotiation Skills, covering 328 bipartite representatives (38% female); and ii. Outreached 46 unionized factories providing training on Trade Union Administration, covering 115 factory-level TU representatives (43% female). iii. Expectation to outreach 123 unionized RMG factories) with training programs to promote (a) Collective Bargaining and Negotiation Skills; and (b) Trade Union Administration by 2021 (tbc).
2. B. During the reporting period, DoL master trainers outreached 420 RMG factories (including 96 unionized factories) with training of Managing Labour Relations, which is reported in BGD 227 (under COVID-19 Training Package).
3. Publicly accessible database developed by DoL to facilitate extracting data and analyzing the growth of Trade Unions (TU) and supporting the efficient processing of registration of TUs. The database includes cases brought to the labour judiciary for remedy by TUs, collective bargaining agreements, information on formation and functions of the Participation Committee, investigation and remediation of complaints regarding Unfair Labour Practices and Anti-Union Discrimination, as well as cases of conciliation recorded and resolved. The database will better equip DoL and labour constituents for reports or statistical analyses.
4. (Virtual) trainings equipped workers and employers at the workplace level with tools to manage labour relations and manage return to work in the RMG sector. 1. ILO provided technical support through the ITC-ILO Turin Centre developing training material and delivering certified training to paralegals as well as refreshers training.
2. A. With the support of Sweden and Denmark, ILO provided trainings to the workers developing training materials on enterprise-level workplace cooperation and collective bargaining.
2. B. With the top-up resources of Sweden, ILO provided support to the Department of Labour (DOL) to train workers on Managing Labour Relations during COVID-19 period.
3. With the support of Sweden and Denmark, ILO supported DoL to develop a Publicly Accessible Database.
4. ILO initiated an RMG Learning Hub to deliver coordinated capacity building support to the industry, including representatives from factory management (e.g. HR, compliance, welfare), Trade Union (TU) representatives and selected worker-management representatives of Participation Committees (PC), Safety Committees (SC), Enterprise Level COVID-19 crisis management teams; and other worker-management representatives.
2-day training course held 9-10 Nov. 2020 in the response to the impacts of COVID-19 (30 representatives were trained, (33% female)). These Master trainers–sourced from the Department of Labour (DOL)–conducted further dissemination of the training materials. During Dec. 2020, four trainings on managing labor relations were conducted for 37 factories. In total 156 participants (78 workers & 78 management) participated (41% female).
In June, 2021 a training session on industrial relations with 84 participants from 14 partner factories was conducted. The participants included workers and management representatives from factories with the presence of the trade unions.
In mid-2020, two interactive virtual training sessions were organized; one with Chittagong based trade union representatives and one with Dhaka based representatives in response to COVID-19. In total, 82 trade unions members (51% female) attended.
